spikeFindings: A1 FALSIFIED: @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10.0.0 joins describe/test names with a space while vitest 5 matches on ' > ', so every mutant run executes 0 tests and every covered mutant reports Survived (10/10 on ts/src/guardian/pr-check.ts:894-905). Upstream stryker-js#6210, open.

A2 PARTLY FALSIFIED: the runner forces pool:'threads' and process.chdir() is unavailable there, so 60 of 237 test files fail the initial run. Excluding them makes a mutant only those suites would kill read as survived, which works against F5's <=10% false-survivor target.
assumptions: F6=(b): the shipped slice is scope derivation, the Stryker-report mapper, abstention and suppression rules, `canary guardian mutation` (exit 0/1/3) and the advisory guardian.yml job. The Stryker execution is NOT shipped.
The abstain guard's predicate is vitest-runner > 10.0.0 or vitest major < 5, held in one exported constant (BROKEN_RUNNER_MAX) with its own test.

No StrykerJS devDependency is pinned in this slice: the shipped code never executes it, so pinning would add ~2.4k lockfile lines and 2 moderate qs advisories (via typed-rest-client) for no behavior. The pins land with the follow-up that turns the runner on.
ts/vitest.mutation.config.ts (the thread-unsafe exclusion config Stryker consumes) is deferred to that same follow-up; this slice ships the excluded-file list and its disclosure only.

The mutation job posts its findings through its own CI surface rather than a section inside pr-check's sticky comment: they are separate jobs and cannot share one comment body without overwriting each other.
A run whose only mutant was suppressed abstains rather than reporting all-killed — nothing was killed, so nothing was proved.
Runs on ubuntu-latest only (spec A4); mutants capped at 150, deterministically sampled, with the denominator always stated (D7/F4).

closingKeywordWhy: Refs, not Closes. Spec success criteria 1 (the #484 regression case), 3 (p90 runtime across 20 PRs) and 7 (the exit-criterion evidence window) all require a runner that actually kills mutants, which stryker-js#6210 prevents. Closing #486 here would mark the issue done on a check that can currently only abstain.
